verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling wheezy and short of breath starting about two days ago after house cleaning with dust exposure: 'it started, like, about two days ago... I was, like, cleaning the house. And, like, um, all this dust came out of the, the carpet... two days later. Still not gonna be better... I'm feeling like a little bit, uh, uh, short of breath.'
Wheeze onset and nocturnal worsening are described: 'so, it started after maybe, uh, an hour or so' (after cleaning) and 'it get's a bit worse, um, at night, I find.'

Patient states both shortness of breath and difficulty completing sentences: 'I'm feeling like a little bit, uh, uh, short of breath' and 'when I'm... talking... to my friends, I start finding that... I'm unable to, complete my sentences.'
Patient denies pleuritic pain and dizziness: to deep breath pain, 'Mmm, no, no. No pain.' and to dizziness, 'Uh, no. No dizziness. Uh, none of that.'
Adequate oral intake is noted: 'have you been eating and drinking OK, particularly water?' / 'Yeah, yeah. I think I'm having, like, you know, four or five glasses a day. Yeah.'
No medication taken for current wheeze: 'have you taken anything for the wheeze?' / 'Uh, no. No, I haven't actually.'

History of childhood asthma with occasional exercise-induced symptoms now: 'I used to have, like, a bit of, um, asthma, uh, as a child... sometimes when I, um, run for, like, long periods, it can, it can start up a bit.'
Seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) in summer: 'also in the summer I sometimes get, um, hay fever.'
Asthma inhaler from a few months ago, details not specified: 'I have, uh, I have, like, an asthma inhaler. I use that.' and later 'I think I might have one from, like, a couple of months ago.'
No current antihistamine use: for hay fever meds, 'Not really.' and later 'I don't have any antihistamines at home, unfortunately.'

Transcript addresses general allergies ('apart from this, do you know if you're allergic to anything?' / 'not that I know of.') but does not mention drug allergies or NKDA specifically. Stating 'No known drug allergies' adds specificity not documented.
Access to GP within minutes' drive: 'How far are you away from a doctor's surgery at the moment?' / 'they may be minutes' drive away.'

Doctor suspects asthma vs allergy triggered by dust: 'given you've got a history of asthma and hay fever. This could be one of two things. But, we want to rule out asthma or an allergy first.' and earlier discussion of dust exposure as trigger.

Urgent in-person assessment and pulse oximetry are planned; other tests are implied but not named: 'what you'll need is visit one of our clinics, so we can do some more tests... use a small device on your finger, to check the amount of oxygen in your blood.' Mention of 'do some more tests' could reasonably include exam/peak flow but these are not explicitly named.
There is no instruction to use a SABA inhaler at home; inhaler possession is only discussed in history: 'I have, like, an asthma inhaler. I use that.' No plan is made to use it before assessment.

Doctor advises starting OTC antihistamine en route or via prescription: 'if you've got something, like an antihistamine... I would take one' and 'You might be able to get one on your way to the doctor's surgery. If not, they can prescribe you one.'

'Consider' oral steroids after assessment matches: patient says 'I have, before, taken steroids for asthma.' Doctor: 'you may need to take some steroids now. But... we won't be able to know until we've done those tests first.'
No safety-net advice about specific red-flag symptoms (worsening SOB, cyanosis, etc.) is given in the transcript.

Doctor will send a letter via the app for same-day GP assessment: 'I'm gonna write a letter for your GP, just to let him know what's happened. And, the consultation with the GP in person shouldn't take too long.' and 'you should get the letter over the app. And then... you can take yourself to the GP.'
